$comment: Label vocabulary /port:init creates in a managed repository: the port app's seven labels.
Each entry names the module that owns it, mirroring port.config.json's modules keys
plus the `core` sentinel for a label that is always created. No module currently gates
a label — every entry below is `core` — but the field stays as a designed extension
point for a future optional label, not dead weight.
`key` is the port.config.json `labels` or `states` key. `name` is the default string,
which a repository may override there. Agents read the configured name, never these
defaults directly.
`role` is one of marker / in-flight / gate / terminal. It is the machine-readable
authority the rendered workflows' blocking-label list is derived from — the in-flight
and gate labels — not merely documentation.
`palette` is the pipeline phase a label belongs to — plan, implement, review, revise,
needs-you or done — or null for the marker. One palette is one hue, shared by the label
here, the desktop app's Board pill and its sidebar dot.
Each label's colour is exactly the app's light-theme dot for its palette (`theme.css`),
so GitHub and the app share one hex. The marker is neutral, off the palette, and wears
the app's navy accent (`--brand`).
`previousColors` lists every colour port has shipped for the label this one replaced or
carried over, so /port:init can tell a label port coloured from one the repository
coloured itself, and recolour only the former.

labels.name: port
labels.description: The port pipeline owns this item

labels.name: needs you
labels.description: Gate: the pipeline is waiting on a person

labels.name: planning
labels.description: In flight: a plan is being researched

labels.name: approved
labels.description: Terminal: findings are at or under the bar, a human merges
